In hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts the result is typed as HubspotToken (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`), but a Response has no access_token/refresh_token, so the unchanged downstream usage persists undefined tokens to prisma.credential.update. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff; only trigger condition depends on env config.

judged_text: In sync mode `hubspotRefreshToken` is an unawaited fetch Response object, but the unchanged downstream code reads `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token` and `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` and persists the result, writing undefined tokens into the credential key. First Hubspot token refresh under credential sync replaces a working credential with access_token: undefined — Hubspot calendar sync breaks for every synced user and the corrupted key is persisted via prisma.credential.update.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sync mode is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), the function executes `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object (not `await response.json()` / parsed token data). In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and downstream logic (not changed in the diff) will treat it like a token object. Under sync mode it will instead be a `Response`, so properties like `access_token` / `refresh_token` will be `undefined`, leading to broken refresh behavior and likely persisting bad credential data if the existing code updates prisma with those fields. The finding’s “unawaited” wording is slightly off (the fetch is awaited), but the core defect (returning a `Response` where token data is expected) is directly shown by the diff.
